games.summary: This is a defense-versus-offense-in-flux game, and the Rams' side of it is sturdier. Los Angeles has a top-two defense against both the pass and the run and keeps Stafford clean, while Green Bay's rushing attack has been the worst in the league by EPA and its third-down offense has been brutal. The wrinkle is the Rams' receiver room: with Nacua and Adams both on injured reserve, Konata Mumpfield is the nominal WR1 on a small sample, and Stafford will lean on tight ends and the run game. Green Bay's best path is a pass rush that finishes plays, especially if Micah Parsons is cleared. The structure still tilts to Los Angeles, mainly in the trenches and on third down.

details.scheme: Los Angeles pairs the league's second-best pass defense (-0.085) and run defense (-0.114) with a line that allows only 3.8% sacks. Green Bay's run game is the worst in football (-0.174/play) and its third-down offense is -0.359 per play, the widest single gap on this game's board. The Rams' own receiver room is depleted (Nacua and Adams on IR), so the Packers' best chance is a pass rush that gets home (7.1% sack rate) and Parsons' return.

games.summary: This game is about two quarterbacks nobody can fully trust: Tommy DeVito for New England, with Drake Maye out, and Justin Herbert, who is in the concussion protocol. Even with that uncertainty, the season data points one way. The Chargers' offense is the league's worst, and their offensive line has allowed 11 percent sacks, which is the single widest lane in this matchup. New England's offense isn't good either, and with A.J. Brown doubtful and DeVito's small sample, it's likely a low-scoring game where one big mistake decides it. The Patriots' pass rush against the Chargers' line is the one structural edge.

details.scheme: The league's worst offense (LAC -0.135/play, #32; pass O -0.154) and the worst-protecting line (11.0% sacks allowed) host a Patriots team that gets to the passer (7.6%). games.summary: Arizona's pass defense is the worst in the league, and Washington has a quarterback in Jayden Daniels who can exploit it. The Commanders' offense is average, but against this Cardinals secondary that's enough to move the ball. Arizona is down a quarterback (Beck's back is a question, and Josh Johnson played last week), has lost its top receiver and running back, and was beaten 34-7 by Kansas City. The only reasons for caution are Washington's shortened week after Monday night and the travel. The pass and third-down numbers still lean clearly to Washington.

games.summary: San Francisco has the league's best offense and a quarterback playing at an elite level, and it just beat Minnesota 35-10. Seattle's strength is a top-five pass defense, and Jaxon Smith-Njigba is the most productive receiver on that side, but the Seahawks' run game ranks near the bottom and their offensive line is thin (Nelson doubtful, Cross and Lucas questionable). If Darnold can't go, Drew Lock has been more efficient than Darnold, which narrows the gap. San Francisco's loss of McKivitz at right tackle is the one real structural concern. The matchup still leans San Francisco by one of the bigger margins this week.

games.summary: Neither team is efficient on offense, so this is a game of who gives it away less. Cleveland's offense is below average and its line allows a lot of sacks, but Las Vegas' defense is one of the league's worst against both pass and run and doesn't rush the passer well enough to take advantage. Mendoza has produced some big games as a rookie, but his season numbers are below average, and the Raiders' offense will depend on whether Brock Bowers is healthy. The Browns have the better defense and a small structural edge, but it's close.

games.summary: This is the most even game on the slate. Tampa Bay has the best pass defense in the league, but its offense has been poor, and a line that allows nine percent sacks is a problem against any pass rush. Carolina has the stronger offense on paper, with Bryce Young and Tetairoa McMillan playing well, but the Panthers don't get to the quarterback much and their third-down offense is poor against this kind of defense. Tampa Bay's secondary is banged up (Winfield, Morrison and Parrish all questionable), which could swing it. It's a game that comes down to a few plays.
